title: Job classes that were paid for a year or two and then vanished
question: Which job classes appear in the payroll for only one or two fiscal years, who held them, and where did the holder go?
finding: 17 job classes were paid in only one or two consecutive fiscal years between 2014 and 2025 and never again; 12 of them had a single holder. Together they were paid $2.4 million. 8 of the 17 carry the tag OCII in their title, a block of classes that entered the file together in fiscal 2015.
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2013 to 2026. Listed: classes whose whole presence is one fiscal year or two consecutive ones, starting after 2013 and ending before 2026. For single-holder classes from 2017 on, the holder’s job the year before and the year after is read from the payroll by name, under the matching rules. Ranked by total pay.
limits: A short-lived class is often an administrative device: a transitional class for a department head who is leaving or arriving, a holding class while a reorganisation is finished, staff taken over from another agency, or a class that was renumbered. Where the holder moved into an ordinary class afterwards, the short-lived class was probably one of these. The classification record would say why each was opened and closed.
